answer: An agent economy can require new identities to post a bond that is locked until they complete useful work verified by independent counterparties. Reputation and access grow only as that bond survives disputes; splitting one agent into a hundred accounts therefore requires funding a hundred bonds, not merely changing names. A marble trader crossing the tundra to reach a harbor still faces the same rule: each claimed identity ties up capital, and proven fraud forfeits it. The attacker pays in scarce funds and loses them when caught.
